scope: COV-013/019x: complete native intensive/emphatic auxiliary source preservation and individual regressions under existing runtime policy. No new engine or filter. Source-supported broader licenses, lexical subsets, semantic/register, full-article and independent Korean-language review remain open.

source_findings.finding: The original -아 빠지다 note says the preceding vowel is not ㅏ/ㅗ, while the headword and native 달아/잘아/낡아 groups contradict that condition. Preserve the complete original source; do not silently correct it or use the note as forbidden gold.

The -어 빠지다 expression note specifies adjectives but its complete native groups include 썩다 and 늙다, which have lexical verb entries. The auxiliary note explicitly admits some verbs and adjectives. A blanket adjective-only restriction would lose native paths.
Some-verb or some-verb/adjective notes specify lexical subsets. Dictionary POS alone cannot prove all lexical pairs semantically suitable.

Native notes give verb attachment and distinct 고 versus 어 connectors. Preserve independent lexical homonyms, later-owner class changes, and unknown lexical heads separately from auxiliary-role judgments.

KRDict classifies the intensive auxiliary as 보조 동사 and specifies adjective attachment. Do not reclassify the original source or assume its note exhausts the semantic verb subset. Primary research abstract consultation is recorded separately; the full article remains unreviewed.

The original GSD 줄서먹는 row is 줄+아서+먹+는 (VV+EC+VX+ETM), yielding gold 줄다+먹다, and remains an exact before miss. Keep the entire sentence, literal row, source connector and mismatch. Do not silently repair 서 or join another word to force recovery.

Joined candidate analysis is tolerant recovery, not a spelling recommendation.

primary_consultation.title: 한국어 ‘-어 죽다’ 구성에 대한 연구
primary_consultation.access: Complete primary metadata and Korean/English author abstracts reviewed; full 26-page article not yet retrieved.
primary_consultation.finding: The author abstract distinguishes literal death and scalar use; it reports some psychological intransitive verbs as well as adjectives, and contextual mood/person/negative restrictions with 없다 exceptions. No unseen article examples, blanket mood/person/negative exclusions, or POS reclassification are asserted.

primary_consultation.access: Primary metadata and Korean/English abstracts reviewed; full article not yet retrieved.
primary_consultation.finding: The Korean abstract characterizes state-predicate attachment as usual, whereas the English abstract says only state verbs. Preserve this difference rather than extracting a universal predicate exclusion; lexical state/change classes differ from dictionary verb/adjective POS.

primary_consultation.title: -었-과 결합하는 보조용언의 문법화와 의미적 특성: -고 앉다, -고 자빠지다, -어 빠지다, -어 터지다를 중심으로
primary_consultation.author: Lee, Keumhee
primary_consultation.access: Primary publisher metadata and abstract reviewed; full article not yet retrieved.
primary_consultation.finding: The author abstract reports both state and change predicates in these past-bearing constructions and emphasizes speaker disapproval. Past-bearing discourse observations do not prove obligatory past in every raw auxiliary use or a universal verb exclusion.

primary_consultation.author: 목지선

primary_consultation.finding: The investigator reports that some state-predicate auxiliary uses depend on following clauses, including trial 보다 and 놓다.
